text.p: These are the headlines for selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Gardens left scrambling over scandal: Cliff Fletcher to meet police today, vows internal investigation of widening sex-abuse allegations.
- Mike Harris reinstates health minister: Privacy watchdog clears Jim Wilson.
- Jean Chretien lengthens NATO list: Canada will endorse Romania as well as Czeck Republic, Poland and Hungary.
- Police kill man aboard Toronto bus: TTC reported woman being attacked.
- Foes maul Tory MPPs at pro-megacity meetings: If the government hoped to draw audiences that supported its plan for a unified Toronto, it failed miserably.
- TSE queries Bre-X ownership: Seeks clarification of whether company did - or didn't - own 90 percent of Busang project.
- David Walsh disputed on stake's saleability: Hasan insists first dibs go to partners.
- Ontario Hydro vows to allow U.S. sales: Seeks reciprocal deal in America.
- Miner linked to mercenaries: DiamondWorks' shareholder acts as agent for security firm.
- Pools bid C$172 million for UGG: Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators make all-cash offer for United Grain Growers, but bid may activate company's freshly minted poison pill.
- Avenor scrambles to rework its Repap offer.
